primary_citation: Cal. Civil Code §§1798-1798.78 (Information Practices Act of 1977, Stats. 1977, Ch. 709, SB 1983, effective 1978-07-01)
short_title: California Information Practices Act (IPA) — State Agency Records: Access, Amendment, and Civil Remedy
one_line_rule: California state agencies must maintain accurate records and cannot disclose personal information without authorization; individuals may access, inspect, and amend their records, and sue for damages when agency failures cause adverse effects — $200 floor without willfulness; individual employees face $2,500 per willful disclosure.

case_law.key_rule: §1798.53 individual employee liability: $2,500 per willful disclosure; no government entity immunity for individual employees; cumulative with §1798.45 agency liability

dds_application.jurisdictional_status: DDS is a CDSS unit (California state agency) — IPA applies. DDS also acts as SSA contractor — federal Privacy Act applies via SSA. Dual-track: IPA amendment demands to CDSS/DDS; federal Privacy Act amendment demands to SSA.
dds_application.amendment_pathway: §1798.34 inspection request → review file → §1798.35 amendment demand identifying false contact dates → agency must respond within 30 days → §1798.45 civil action if refused
dds_application.phantom_contacts: False DDS contact dates (9/18/2019, 3/23/2020, 12/17/2020) = IPA §1798.35 amendment targets; adverse effect = disability denial; actual damages = lost benefit payments; $200 floor no willfulness required
dds_application.individual_liability: DDS examiners who entered false dates = §1798.53 candidates; $2,500 per willful disclosure + actual damages; accounting of disclosures under §1798.40 identifies responsible individuals
